$schema_note: The CONTRACT for PaperTree geometry. Consumed by document-ir/geometry.spec in BOTH TypeScript and Python, so the two languages are checked against one recording rather than against each other. Regenerate with `uv run --python 3.12 --with pymupdf python packages/document-ir/test/fixtures-pdf/generate.py`.

oracles.fixture_vectors: MuPDF. Markers are painted by a raw PDF content stream, read back with page.get_drawings(), divided by /UserUnit and mapped with page.rotation_matrix - a second, independently implemented coordinate pipeline.
oracles.everything_else: hand arithmetic, written as literals in generate.py with the working shown in the comment beside each entry. Nothing here was produced by running geometry.ts or geometry.py.

spec.ir_space: PDF DEFAULT USER SPACE units (1/72 in); origin TOP-LEFT of the page's post-rotation CROP rect; y grows DOWNWARD; /Rotate already applied; coordinates relative to the crop rect's own origin so a CropBox offset cannot leak in; /UserUnit DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED. Identical to ADR-001 Amendment 1 'COORDINATE FRAME', which is what the block id is computed in.
spec.normalise: u = raw_x - crop.x0 ; v = crop.y1 - raw_y ; then rotate clockwise inside cw x ch: rot 0 -> (u, v) [cw x ch]; rot 90 -> (ch - v, u) [ch x cw]; rot 180 -> (cw - u, ch - v) [cw x ch]; rot 270 -> (v, cw - u) [ch x cw]. The effective crop box is CropBox INTERSECT MediaBox, corner-ordered (PDF 1.7 14.11.2); an absent /CropBox defaults to the MediaBox.
spec.viewport: s = zoom * user_unit ; W = page_width * s ; H = page_height * s ; rot 0 -> (x*s, y*s) on a W x H surface; rot 90 -> (H - y*s, x*s) on H x W; rot 180 -> (W - x*s, H - y*s) on W x H; rot 270 -> (y*s, W - x*s) on H x W. `rotation` here is the VIEWER's extra rotation on top of the page's own /Rotate, which is already baked into page_width/page_height and every stored polygon.
spec.user_unit_boundary: /UserUnit is RECORDED in the IR and APPLIED ONLY in the viewport transform. Amendment 1 pins it out of the id's coordinate frame; geometry.spec requires the viewport transform to handle it. Both hold at once because they are different spaces. MEASURED CAVEAT: Amendment 1 justifies the rule with 'it is what MuPDF's page.rect gives' - that is FALSE as of PyMuPDF 1.28 / MuPDF 1.29, which scales page.rect and every extracted coordinate by /UserUnit while leaving page.rotation_matrix unscaled. The rule stands; the justification does not, and a PyMuPDF-based parser must divide /UserUnit out exactly once before storing.
spec.polygon_conventions: bbox == polygon extent, ALWAYS (schema + semantic validator rule 1); rings are NOT closed (do not repeat the first vertex); signed area is the shoelace sum halved, positive for a ring that reads clockwise on screen in this y-down frame; point-in-polygon is even-odd with the boundary tested explicitly first and INCLUSIVE by default; polygon intersection and bbox intersection both count boundary contact as intersecting.
spec.union_of_line_rects: Two line rects join one run iff their x-extents overlap by more than horizontal_overlap_tolerance AND their y-intervals overlap or are separated by at most vertical_gap_tolerance; connectivity is transitive. Each run becomes ONE staircase polygon whose horizontal band edges sit at the midpoint of each inter-line gap. A selection spanning two columns therefore returns TWO polygons and never a bounding box across the gutter. Rects with non-positive width or height are dropped. Output is sorted by (top, left).

how_to_use: 1. `page_frames`: normalise_page_frame(raw) MUST equal `frame` field for field.

2. `normalisation_vectors` / `normalise_rect_vectors`: the named frame's normalise_point / normalise_rect MUST equal `expected` exactly (these are all exact binary64 values), and denormalise_point MUST return the raw point.
3. `viewport_vectors`: pdf_to_viewport MUST equal `viewport_point`, viewport_size MUST equal `surface`, and viewport_to_pdf MUST invert.
4. `roundtrip_grid`: every (page, zoom, rotation, user_unit, point) combination must round-trip with max abs error < max_abs_error_pt. This is the acceptance criterion.

6. `fixture_vectors`: open the PDF in `test/fixtures-pdf/`, read /MediaBox, /CropBox, /Rotate and /UserUnit from the page dictionary, build the frame, normalise each raw marker rect, and compare with `expected_marker_bboxes` - which came from MuPDF.

normalisation_vectors.label: norm:rot0:crop-top-left
normalisation_vectors.why: the crop box's top-left corner IS the IR origin (u=0, v=720-720=0)

normalisation_vectors.label: norm:rot0:outside-crop-origin
normalisation_vectors.why: the PDF origin is OUTSIDE the crop box: u=-72, v=720. Not clamped.

normalisation_vectors.label: norm:rot90:crop-top-left
normalisation_vectors.why: u=0,v=0 -> (630-0, 0). Rotating clockwise sends the top-left to the top-right.

normalisation_vectors.label: norm:userunit:interior
normalisation_vectors.why: if this were [250,250] the impl applied /UserUnit - Amendment 1 forbids it

normalisation_vectors.label: norm:reversed-corners:crop-top-left
normalisation_vectors.why: corner order in the file is irrelevant

viewport_vectors.label: vp:rot90:zoom1:origin
viewport_vectors.why: H - 0 = 630, so the page's top-left lands on the surface's top-RIGHT

viewport_vectors.label: vp:userunit:rot0:zoom1
viewport_vectors.why: s = 1*2.5. The SAME point normalised to [100,100] in IR space (see norm:userunit:interior) renders at 250 - that is the whole UserUnit boundary.

roundtrip_grid.why: the named acceptance test: document-ir/geometry.spec. Points deliberately include the page corners AND points outside the crop box (negative, and beyond width/height) - a transform that only works inside the page is not a transform.

points.why: the notch. A bounding box would say True - that is highlight bleed.

polygon_vectors.label: poly:bowtie
polygon_vectors.why: self-intersecting: validator rule G6 WARNs on this and G6's area check ERRORs

points.why: the crossing point, on both edges

polygon_vectors.label: poly:counter-clockwise-square
polygon_vectors.why: reversing the ring flips the SIGN and leaves the absolute area alone

polygon_vectors.label: poly:negative-coords
polygon_vectors.why: IR space is not the positive quadrant - see media_box on a cropped page

intersection_vectors.label: isect:two-columns
intersection_vectors.why: THE case. Two column blocks on the same lines must not intersect.

intersection_vectors.label: isect:touching-edges
intersection_vectors.why: boundary contact counts - stated so the two languages cannot disagree

intersection_vectors.label: isect:nested
intersection_vectors.why: containment has no edge crossing; an edge-only test would answer False

intersection_vectors.label: isect:staircase-notch
intersection_vectors.why: the probe sits in the staircase's notch. Bounding boxes DO overlap here.

intersection_vectors.label: isect:crossing-no-vertex-inside
intersection_vectors.why: a plus sign: no vertex of either is inside the other, only edges cross

line_union_vectors.label: union:two-column-selection
line_union_vectors.why: THE named operation. A selection spanning both columns returns TWO polygons, so nothing is ever painted across the gutter (findings.md highlight bleed).

line_union_vectors.label: union:single-rect
line_union_vectors.why: one line is a rectangle, wound clockwise on screen starting at the top-right

line_union_vectors.label: union:paragraph-gap-splits
line_union_vectors.why: an 18 pt vertical gap exceeds the 2 pt tolerance, so these are two regions

line_union_vectors.label: union:same-band-fragments-merge
line_union_vectors.why: two word runs on one line: same run, overlapping y -> one band [54,100,292,113]

line_union_vectors.label: union:short-last-line-still-joins
line_union_vectors.why: band edge (112+113)/2 = 112.5; the short line joins by x-overlap of 36 pt

line_union_vectors.label: union:degenerate-rects-dropped
line_union_vectors.why: zero-width and zero-height rects are not regions and are dropped

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:rotate-0
fixture_vectors.why: the baseline: /Rotate 0, CropBox == MediaBox, no /UserUnit. Matches 100% of the real corpus, so it is the case that proves the fixtures agree with reality.

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:rotate-90
fixture_vectors.why: /Rotate 90. The corpus has none; P9 measured the cost of a wrong frame at 99.93%.

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:cropbox-offset
fixture_vectors.why: a CropBox strictly inside the MediaBox with a non-zero origin - the case DESIGN.md D23 exists for, and the one that silently offsets every polygon when unhandled.

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:userunit
fixture_vectors.why: /UserUnit 2.5. The stored frame must be IDENTICAL to the same page without it (Amendment 1 pins UserUnit out of the id frame); only the viewport scale changes.

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:negative-mediabox
fixture_vectors.why: a MediaBox with negative coordinates. The corpus has zero negative coordinates; the normalised origin must be the crop rect's own corner, not (0, 0).

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:cropbox-outside-mediabox
fixture_vectors.why: a CropBox that escapes the MediaBox. PDF 1.7 14.11.2 says the visible page is the INTERSECTION; a reader that trusts the CropBox verbatim gets the page size wrong.

fixture_vectors.label: fixture:combined
fixture_vectors.why: all four at once: negative MediaBox, offset CropBox, /Rotate 270, /UserUnit 1.5. This is where implementations break, so it is the one that must be in the suite.

pymupdf_version: PyMuPDF 1.28.0: Python bindings for the MuPDF 1.29.0 library.
